message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that is equipped with an NVIDIA GPU (the closest supported GPU to an RTX A6000 is the **NVIDIA A100‑80GB**).  
If you truly need an RTX A6000 you’ll have to wait until Google Cloud adds that GPU family – at the moment it isn’t available in the public catalog.

---

## 1️⃣  Prerequisites

| Item | How to set it up |
|------|------------------|
| **Project ID** | `PROJECT_ID` – replace with your own GCP project ID |
| **Zone** | `ZONE` – e.g. `us-central1-a` |
| **Service account key** | JSON key file for a service account that has the **Compute Admin** role (`roles/compute.admin`) |
| **Billing enabled** | Make sure billing is attached to the project |
| **GPU API enabled** | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` (this automatically enables GPU support) |

> **Tip:** If you’re using the **gcloud CLI** you can skip the service‑account key step by running the commands from a machine that already has the `gcloud` SDK installed and is authenticated with a user that has the required permissions.

---

## 2️⃣  Using the **gcloud CLI**

```bash
# 1. Set variables
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="gpu-ubuntu-instance"

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="200GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-a100-80gb,count=1" \
  --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: custom init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 200 GB |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one NVIDIA A100‑80GB GPU |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Terminate the instance if the host is rebooted (GPU instances are not live‑migrated) |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart on crash |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script on first boot |

> **Note:** If you need a different GPU family (e.g. `nvidia-tesla-v100`), change the `type=` value accordingly.

---

## 3️⃣  Using the **REST API** (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g. from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), here’s the exact payload you would POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/zones/ZONE/instances
Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "gpu-ubuntu-instance",
  "machineType": "zones/ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "zones/ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "zones/ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a100-80gb"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-8"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to obtain `ACCESS_TOKEN`

```bash
gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
```

or use OAuth 2.0 flow to get a bearer token.

---

## 4️⃣  Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify the GPU attachment:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe gpu-ubuntu-instance \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --format="json(accelerators)"
```

You should see something like:

```json
{
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a100-80gb"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 5️⃣  Common pitfalls & troubleshooting

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **“GPU quota exceeded”** | Request a GPU quota increase in the GCP console → IAM & Admin → Quotas. |
| **Instance fails to start** | Check the serial port logs: `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output gpu-ubuntu-instance --zone=$ZONE`. |
| **GPU not visible inside the VM** | Ensure you installed the NVIDIA driver inside the VM. You can add a startup script that runs `sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-525` or use the official NVIDIA CUDA image. |
| **Billing error** | Verify that billing is enabled for the project. |

---

## 6️⃣  Wrap‑up

* **gcloud CLI** is the simplest way to spin up a GPU instance.  
* **REST API** gives you programmatic control if you’re integrating into a larger system.  
* Replace `nvidia-a100-80gb` with another accelerator type if you need a different GPU family.  

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
